name: State trial-court case filings by county, court level and case type: Texas, Washington, Maryland, Indiana, Wisconsin, Virginia, Pennsylvania, Oregon, West Virginia, Nebraska, Maine, California, Louisiana and Hawaii
description: How many cases are filed in state trial courts, by county, court level and case group, from each state court system's own published statistics. Texas (Office of Court Administration): district, constitutional county and statutory county courts, fiscal years 2023–24 and 2024–25, with district-court filings by case type. Washington (Administrative Office of the Courts): superior courts and district and municipal courts (criminal, civil, domestic, probate, juvenile, traffic, DUI, protection orders, small claims), calendar year 2025. Maryland (Judiciary data dashboard): circuit-court filings by case type and District Court filings (landlord-tenant, civil, criminal, DUI, traffic citations, peace orders), fiscal years 2012 to 2025. Indiana (Office of Judicial Administration): circuit and superior court new filings by Rule 8 case type (felony, misdemeanor, tort, collection, small claims, eviction, foreclosure, domestic relations, estates, juvenile), calendar year 2025 (provisional) beside 2024. Wisconsin (Director of State Courts Office): circuit-court cases opened by category, felony to juvenile, 2020 to 2025. Virginia (Office of the Executive Secretary): circuit, general district and juvenile and domestic relations district courts by locality (county or independent city), calendar year 2025. Pennsylvania (Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts): courts of common pleas in all 67 counties, civil cases by type (motor-vehicle and other torts, mass torts, malpractice, contract and debt, landlord-tenant, foreclosure) and criminal, protection from abuse, support, custody, divorce, juvenile, adoption and guardianship cases, calendar year 2024. Oregon (Oregon Judicial Department): circuit courts in all 36 counties, calendar year 2025. West Virginia (Supreme Court of Appeals): circuit, family and magistrate courts in all 55 counties, calendar year 2025. Nebraska (Judicial Branch): county and district courts in all 93 counties and the separate juvenile courts of three of them, fiscal year 2024–25. Maine (Judicial Branch): superior courts, unified criminal dockets and district courts in all 16 counties, fiscal years 2021–22 to 2025–26. California (Judicial Council): superior courts in all 58 counties (motor-vehicle and other injury, limited civil, eviction, small claims, felony, misdemeanor, traffic, marital, parentage, domestic violence, child support, juvenile delinquency and dependency, guardianship, other probate, mental health), fiscal year 2024–25. Louisiana (Supreme Court of Louisiana, Judicial Administrator's Office): district courts in 61 of the state's 64 parishes (civil, criminal, traffic and juvenile cases), calendar year 2025 beside 2024 where the 2024 report's row matches. Hawaii (Hawaii State Judiciary): circuit courts in all four circuits, each mapped to its county (motor-vehicle and other injury, contract, foreclosure, probate proceedings, circuit criminal cases), fiscal year 2024–25. Every record keeps the state's own category names and the numbers added into each group (components), and carries a harmonized group and the practice areas it bears on, so a county's filings can be read as demand for personal injury, family, landlord-tenant, small claims and debt, probate, criminal and DUI, juvenile and traffic work. In every source the counties add up to the state's own printed total where it prints one (Texas, Washington, Indiana, Wisconsin, Virginia, Pennsylvania, Oregon, West Virginia, Nebraska, Hawaii), Louisiana's parish records are the parishes whose rows add up to the printed district totals and its state row is the state's printed total, and the state rows for Maryland are the sum of the counties. Every record carries its FIPS code (the state's on a state row, the county's on a county row) so it joins Census and other county data. Counts only: no lawyer or firm is listed or ranked.

distribution.name: state-courts.csv
distribution.description: Every record, one row each (RFC 4180, UTF-8). Columns are described in README.txt.

distribution.name: state-courts.json
distribution.description: Every record with its full sources, under a meta envelope (credit line, DOI, license).

distribution.name: state-courts-values.csv
distribution.description: The columns listed in README.txt as being in state-courts-values.csv, one row per id, column and value; join it to state-courts.csv on id.

recordSet.name: state-courts
recordSet.description: The records of State trial-court case filings by county, court level and case type: Texas, Washington, Maryland, Indiana, Wisconsin, Virginia, Pennsylvania, Oregon, West Virginia, Nebraska, Maine, California, Louisiana and Hawaii, one per CSV row.

field.name: id
field.description: Stable record id (never reused)

field.name: state
field.description: Two-letter state code (TX, WA, MD, IN, WI, VA, PA, OR, WV, NE, ME, CA, LA or HI)

field.name: area
field.description: The state code for the whole state, or STATE-COUNTYNAME for a county (uppercase, hyphens for spaces), e.g. WA-KING, MD-BALTIMORE-CITY, VA-RICHMOND-CITY, PA-PHILADELPHIA; a Virginia court serving a city and a county together is one area, e.g. VA-WILLIAMSBURG-CITY-AND-JAMES-CITY

field.name: areaName
field.description: Area name

field.name: areaType
field.description: us, state or cbsa

field.name: fips
field.description: FIPS codes of the area: the 2-digit state code on a state row; on a county row the 5-digit county code, or several codes where one court serves a city and a county together (Virginia)

field.name: courtLevel
field.description: The court level the count is for (Texas: district, constitutional-county or statutory-county; Washington: superior or limited; Maryland: circuit or district; Indiana: trial; Wisconsin: circuit; Virginia: circuit, gdc (general district) or jdr (juvenile and domestic relations district); Pennsylvania: common-pleas; Oregon: circuit; West Virginia: circuit, family or magistrate; Nebraska: county, district or juvenile (separate juvenile courts); Maine: superior, ucd (unified criminal docket) or district; California: superior; Louisiana: district; Hawaii: circuit)

field.name: group
field.description: The group: civil, family, probate, juvenile, criminal, traffic, small-claims or landlord-tenant (Texas: civil, family, juvenile, criminal, felony or misdemeanor)

field.name: measure
field.description: Texas: court level, group and what is counted. Other states: the harmonized group (for example civil-eviction, family-divorce, criminal-dui)

field.name: fy
field.description: The period: a Texas, Maryland, Nebraska, Maine, California or Hawaii fiscal year (e.g. 2024-25) or a calendar year (Washington, Indiana, Wisconsin, Virginia, Pennsylvania, Oregon, West Virginia, Louisiana)

field.name: value
field.description: Cases filed in the period (Texas: added to the docket; Wisconsin: cases opened, the state's Total Opened)

field.name: unit
field.description: Unit of value

field.name: status
field.description: P primary source, S secondary source

field.name: text
field.description: The record in one plain-English sentence

field.name: effectiveFrom
field.description: When the fact took effect (YYYY-MM-DD), if known

field.name: effectiveTo
field.description: When it stopped applying; empty while current

field.name: lastChecked
field.description: The day it was last confirmed (YYYY-MM-DD)

field.name: sourceLabels
field.description: Sources, separated by " | "

field.name: sourceUrls
field.description: Source URLs, in the same order

field.name: confidence
field.description: high, medium or low: computed from status, a second check, age against the refresh cadence and sampling error (rule: /data/#confidence)

field.name: confidenceBasis
field.description: The reasons for the confidence level, in a short phrase
